hypotheses: type (i) geometric fibre, or a connected component of a reduced locally Noetherian balanced+(CE)+(N) base meeting the type-(i) locus
normality of U_alpha for irreducibility and for the FND-0152 identity

finding.statement: On a balanced type-(i) geometric fibre the geometric monodromy image of pi_1^{et}(|L|^{rs})->S_6 is the full symmetric group: the point-line incidence is an irreducible P^1-bundle (transitivity); after deleting the diagonal and the finite coincidence locus over non-normal points of the sextic, the ordered-pair incidence is irreducible and dominant of degree 30 (2-transitivity, hence primitivity); a general tangent line is a simple tangency at a smooth point of the dual curve (a transposition, using characteristic-zero reflexivity of the Gauss map and nonvanishing of the Wronskian of the complete g^2_6); Jordan's theorem then gives S_6, so the ordering torsor is connected. Over any connected component S_alpha of a reduced locally Noetherian balanced+(CE)+(N) base that contains at least one type-(i) geometric fibre, functoriality of pi_1^{et} along U_b -> U_alpha forces H_alpha=S_6, hence Z_alpha is connected; if U_alpha is additionally normal, integral and locally Noetherian then Z_alpha is irreducible, [S_6:H_alpha]=1, and the FND-0152 induction functor is the identity. This computes the monodromy image left open by FND-0148 and FND-0152, but only on components that meet the type-(i) locus. In type (ii) the image lies in a conjugate of the imprimitive wreath product S_2 wr S_3 of order 48 and is not S_6. The statement upgrades nothing to Tate type (FND-0053, FND-0152(ii)), does not apply to algebraic stacks with inertia (FND-0144), and does not determine H_alpha on a purely type-(ii) component.
